meta.what: USACE Formerly Used Defense Sites properties per county, FY2024 inventory: all properties, properties with cleanup projects, and properties with projects not all at site closeout. A program status, not a finding of contamination.
meta.asOf: FUDS inventory, fiscal year 2024 (USACE calls it preliminary)

featureRule.fuds_properties: distinct FUDS property numbers USACE locates in the county: by its county field, or by its point where the field is blank, names no county, or could name more than one (a county-or-independent-city name such as ST LOUIS, or a list) and the point is in one of them
featureRule.fuds_properties_with_projects: of those, STATUS 'Properties with projects' or 'Properties with all projects at site closeout'
featureRule.fuds_properties_with_open_projects: of those, STATUS 'Properties with projects' (not all at site closeout)

source.name: USACE Formerly Used Defense Sites (FUDS), property points

countyOutlines.note: fetched for the point-in-county join only; not committed

counties.source: TIGERweb https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Generalized_ACS2023/State_County/MapServer layer 13 (Counties 20M: the 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico; Connecticut as planning regions); adjacency from https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/county_adjacency/county_adjacency2023.txt.

meta.join: USACE's COUNTY string by name (lib/places/countyJoin.ts, failing closed); where it is blank or names no county, USACE's point in a TIGERweb ACS2023 500K county outline of the property's state; where it could name more than one county (a name that is both a county and an independent city, such as ST LOUIS, FAIRFAX, RICHMOND or BALTIMORE, or a list of counties), the point decides when it is in one of them (e.g. B07MO0988, 'ST LOUIS', to St. Louis city 29510; counts.joinMethod.pointOnlyByNameReason), and otherwise those counties are null; with neither, a single name one edit from exactly one county of the state (a misspelling such as SCHUYKILL; each listed in nearNames); never the nearest county. Where both are given and differ, the name is kept and the pair is listed in pointDisagreements (as NPL keeps and lists far matches): a large property's point can sit in a neighbouring county.
meta.zeroRule: A county in counties.json that is not in `places` and not in `nullPlaces` has 0 for every feature, and that 0 means no property USACE locates in this county: a true 0 for located properties, because the FUDS inventory is USACE's complete list of program properties. Properties for which USACE publishes a state but no county string, and no point in a county (no point at all, or a point at sea or on a remote island), are in no county's count; they are listed in `unlocated` by state (265 of 9971 in-scope properties, 2.7%), and a county's 0 does not rule them out. The strict alternative, every county of a state with an unlocated property null, gives an observed share of 0.405 instead of this rule's 0.9957; it is in counts.strictRule for reference. This rule is approved (zeroRuleStatus).
meta.zeroRuleStatus: approved: Cam decided on 2026-10-16 to keep the zeros (0 = no property USACE locates in this county); counts.strictRule is kept for reference
meta.nullRule: A county an unplaced property could be in is null for every feature (nullPlaces): join:multi_county or join:ambiguous_county_or_city (the counties named, plus the county its point is in when that is another), join:predecessor_county (a county that no longer exists: Census's successors, e.g. Valdez-Cordova to Chugach and Copper River), or join:unplaced_property_in_state (a county string that matches nothing and no point in a county of the state: every county of its state is null). The strict alternative, every county of a state with an unlocated property null too, is reported in counts.strictRule.
